notes.claim: The energy needed to change a material's temperature depends on its mass, its specific heat capacity and the temperature change wanted.
For water, 4,200 J raises 1 kg by 1 °C.
Latent heat is energy that enters or leaves during a phase change without any temperature change, so melting or boiling happens at a steady temperature.
Water's heat of fusion is 334 J/g and its heat of vaporization is 2260 J/g, so boiling away a kilogram takes about 2,260 kJ.

sources.title: Specific heat capacity - Temperature changes and energy - Edexcel - GCSE Physics (Single Science) Revision - Edexcel - BBC Bitesize
sources.quote: The specific heat capacity of water is 4,200 joules per kilogram per degree Celsius (J/kg°C). This means that it takes 4,200 J to raise the temperature of 1 kg of water by 1°C.

sources.title: Specific heat capacity - Energy and heating - AQA - GCSE Physics (Single Science) Revision - AQA - BBC Bitesize
sources.quote: The amount of energy needed depends on: * the mass of the material * the substance of the material ( specific heat capacity ) * the desired temperature change

sources.title: 11.3 Phase Change and Latent Heat - Physics | OpenStax
sources.quote: Because this energy enters or leaves a system during a phase change without causing a temperature change in the system, it is known as latent heat
